name: Galactose metabolism
summary: Liver. Lactose → glucose + galactose; galactose joins glycolysis as glucose-6-phosphate. UDP-galactose 4-epimerase turns the UDP-galactose made by GALT back into UDP-glucose. When the pathway is blocked, aldose reductase makes galactitol, which pulls water into the lens → cataracts.

gal1p.name: Galactose-1-phosphate
gal1p.notes: Accumulates and is toxic in classic galactosemia.

galactitol.name: Galactitol
galactitol.notes: Osmotically active in the lens → cataracts.

galk.name: Galactokinase
galk.notes: Deficiency is mild: galactosemia and galactosuria, infantile cataracts (may present as failure to track objects or develop a social smile).

galt.name: Galactose-1-phosphate uridyltransferase
galt.notes: Deficiency = classic galactosemia (AR): failure to thrive, jaundice, hepatomegaly, intellectual disability, cataracts, E. coli sepsis in neonates. Remove galactose and lactose from the diet.

pgm1.name: Phosphoglucomutase
pgm1.notes: Also links glycogen to glycolysis (G1P ⇌ G6P). Not phosphoglycerate mutase.

ar.name: Aldose reductase
ar.notes: Same enzyme that makes sorbitol from glucose (polyol pathway).

lactase.name: Lactase
lactase.notes: Brush-border enzyme; declines after weaning in most adults → lactose intolerance (osmotic diarrhea, bloating; ↑ breath hydrogen, stool pH <6). Secondary loss after gastroenteritis or celiac disease.

sglt1.name: SGLT1
sglt1.notes: Apical Na⁺-coupled uptake of glucose and galactose into enterocytes (then GLUT2 out to the blood). Fructose uses GLUT5 instead. Brings glucose and galactose into the enterocyte with Na⁺ (secondary active transport).

glut2.name: GLUT2
glut2.notes: Bidirectional, high-capacity: lets galactose out of the enterocyte (basolateral side) and into the hepatocyte.

diseases.name: Galactokinase deficiency
diseases.clue: Infantile cataracts (galactitol) in an otherwise well baby who has trouble tracking objects; galactose in blood and urine.

diseases.name: Classic galactosemia
diseases.clue: Infant vomiting, jaundice, hepatomegaly, cataracts and E. coli sepsis after starting breast milk; galactitol and galactose-1-phosphate build up.
